text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have experienced any severe headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the altered mentation and fever in a patient on haloperidol, I need to rule out life-threatening conditions like Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Do you have any muscle rigidity, high blood pressure, or excessive sweating? I will also check your current temperature and muscle tone.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and autonomic instability (profuse sweating) in the context of haloperidol use is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will now request laboratory tests to confirm this suspicion and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatine_Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated), Complete_Blood_Count: White_Blood_Cell_Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated), Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis, combined with your clinical presentation of fever, rigidity, and altered mentation while on haloperidol, confirm the diagnosis of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
